```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  comment = "#>", collapse = TRUE,
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6, dpi = 120

```

**A shot chart puts every field goal attempt where it was taken, so you can see
a player's or a team's shot diet at a glance.** This article loads a full season
of WNBA and women's college shots from the `wehoop` data releases, draws them on
a regulation court with [`sportyR`](https://sportyR.sportsdataverse.org/), and
builds the standard views: makes and misses, a hexbin density map, shot zones
and field goal percentage (FG%) by zone.

If you are new to `wehoop`, start with
[Getting Started](getting-started-wehoop.html).

## What you'll learn

- Which `wehoop` loaders return shot locations, and which coordinate frame each
  uses.
- How to put every shot on one basket so a half-court chart shows them all.
- How to draw makes and misses for one player, and a hexbin density map for a
  team.
- How to classify shots into zones and compute FG% by zone.
- How to convert WNBA Stats API shot locations with
  `sdvplotR::sdv_court_coords()`, and dress the court in team colors with
  `sdvplotR::sdv_surface()`.

```{r libraries}
library(wehoop)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sportyR)
```

## Which loaders have shot locations?

| Loader | Source | Location columns | Units and origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `load_wnba_shots()` | ESPN play-by-play | `coordinate_x`, `coordinate_y` | Feet, center court at (0, 0), `x` along the court (baskets at about ±41.75), `y` across it (±25) |
| `load_wbb_shots()` | ESPN play-by-play | `coordinate_x`, `coordinate_y` | Same frame as the WNBA loader |
| `load_wnba_stats_shots()` | WNBA Stats API | `x_legacy`, `y_legacy` | Tenths of a foot, origin at the shooter's basket |
| `load_ncaa_wbb_shots()` | stats.ncaa.org play-by-play | none (shot type and outcome only) | |

All three loaders with locations read pre-built season files from GitHub
releases; none of them calls a live API. The ESPN coordinates are already in the
center-court frame that `sportyR::geom_basketball()` draws, so no conversion is
needed. The WNBA Stats API frame needs one, covered
[below](#wnba-stats-api-shots-and-sdv_court_coords).

## Load a season of WNBA shots

```{r load-wnba}
wnba_shots <- load_wnba_shots(seasons = 2025)

wnba_shots |>
  select(athlete_name_1, team_abbrev, type_text, scoring_play, score_value,
         coordinate_x, coordinate_y) |>
  head()
```

The table includes free throws (`type_text` such as "Free Throw - 1 of 2" in the WNBA
feed, "MadeFreeThrow" in the college feed). They are
not field goal attempts and their location is the free throw line, so drop them.

```{r fga}
wnba_fga <- wnba_shots |>
  filter(!grepl("free ?throw", type_text, ignore.case = TRUE))

nrow(wnba_fga)
```

## Put every shot on one basket

Teams switch baskets at halftime, so half of a team's shots sit at each end of
the court. Fold every shot onto the left basket. Reflecting `x` alone would flip
the shooter's left and right, so rotate the court half-turn instead: negate both
coordinates for shots taken at the right-hand basket.

```{r fold}
fold_to_left_basket <- function(shots) {
  shots |>
    mutate(
      x = -abs(coordinate_x),
      y = if_else(coordinate_x > 0, -coordinate_y, coordinate_y),
      # distance in feet from the center of the left basket (41.75 ft from center court)
      shot_distance = sqrt((x + 41.75)^2 + y^2),
      result = if_else(scoring_play, "Made", "Missed")
    )
}

wnba_fga <- fold_to_left_basket(wnba_fga)
```

Every shot now sits on the left half, which
`geom_basketball(display_range = "defense")` draws.

## Makes and misses for one player

The player with the most field goal attempts in the 2025 release:

```{r top-shooter}
top_shooter <- wnba_fga |>
  count(athlete_name_1, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(athlete_name_1)

top_shooter
```

```{r make-miss, fig.alt = "Half-court shot chart of one WNBA player's 2025 field goal attempts, makes in purple and misses in grey."}
player_shots <- wnba_fga |> filter(athlete_name_1 == top_shooter)

geom_basketball("wnba", display_range = "defense") +
  geom_point(
    aes(x, y, color = result),
    data = player_shots, alpha = 0.6, size = 1.8,
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.3, height = 0.3, seed = 1)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Made = "#221A4D", Missed = "grey55")) +
  labs(
    title = paste(top_shooter, "2025 field goal attempts"),
    subtitle = sprintf("%d attempts, %.1f%% made",
                       nrow(player_shots), 100 * mean(player_shots$scoring_play)),
    color = NULL,
    caption = "Data: wehoop::load_wnba_shots()"
  )
```

ESPN records locations on a one-foot grid, so many shots share a point. The
small jitter keeps them from hiding each other.

## Where does a team shoot from? Hexbin density

With thousands of shots, points overlap into a blob. A hexbin chart counts shots
in hexagonal cells instead. This needs the `hexbin` package.

```{r hexbin, fig.alt = "Hexbin shot density map of one WNBA team's 2025 field goal attempts, darker hexagons where more shots were taken."}
team_shots <- wnba_fga |> filter(team_abbrev == "LV")

geom_basketball("wnba", display_range = "defense") +
  geom_hex(aes(x, y), data = team_shots, binwidth = c(2, 2), alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#e8e3f3", high = "#221A4D", trans = "sqrt") +
  labs(
    title = "Las Vegas Aces, 2025: shot density",
    fill = "Attempts",
    caption = "Data: wehoop::load_wnba_shots()"
  )
```

Read a hexbin map by where the dark cells cluster: at the rim, along the
three-point arc, or in the mid-range between them. The zone table below turns
that impression into numbers.

## Shot zones

A zone chart groups shots into areas with similar value. We use five zones,
defined by distance from the basket:

| Zone | Rule (feet from the basket center) |
|---|---|
| Restricted area | under 4 ft |
| Paint | 4 ft to 8 ft |
| Mid-range | 8 ft out to the three-point line |
| Corner three | beyond the line in the straight corner section (within about 14 ft of the baseline, more than 21 ft from the middle of the court) |
| Above-the-break three | beyond the arc, which we take as 22 ft |

The WNBA three-point line is 22 ft 1.75 in at the top of the arc and 22 ft in
the corners; NCAA women's basketball has used the same distance since the
2021-22 season. The zone cut-offs are a simplification, so check them against
the data: a made shot records its point value, so the share of made shots whose
zone agrees with a two or a three tells us how well the rule works.

```{r zones}
add_zone <- function(shots) {
  shots |>
    mutate(
      corner = abs(y) > 21 & x <= -33,
      zone = case_when(
        corner ~ "Corner three",
        shot_distance >= 22 ~ "Above-the-break three",
        shot_distance < 4 ~ "Restricted area",
        shot_distance < 8 ~ "Paint",
        TRUE ~ "Mid-range"
      ),
      zone_is_three = zone %in% c("Corner three", "Above-the-break three"),
      zone = factor(zone, levels = c("Restricted area", "Paint", "Mid-range",
                                     "Corner three", "Above-the-break three"))
    )
}

wnba_fga <- add_zone(wnba_fga)

# Agreement between the zone rule and the recorded value of made shots
wnba_fga |>
  filter(scoring_play) |>
  summarise(agreement = mean(zone_is_three == (score_value == 3)))
```

## FG% by zone

```{r fg-by-zone}
league_zones <- wnba_fga |>
  group_by(zone) |>
  summarise(
    attempts = n(),
    makes = sum(scoring_play),
    fg_pct = makes / attempts,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    share_of_attempts = attempts / sum(attempts),
    points_per_shot = fg_pct * if_else(grepl("three", zone), 3, 2)
  )

league_zones
```

Points per shot (FG% times the shot's point value) is why the corner three and
the restricted area are prized: they return the most per attempt.

Compare one player against the league in each zone:

```{r player-zone-chart, fig.alt = "Half-court chart with one WNBA player's shots colored by zone and labelled with her field goal percentage in each zone."}
# Fixed label positions, one per zone, so labels do not pile up at the rim
label_spots <- tibble(
  zone = levels(wnba_fga$zone),
  x = c(-44, -33, -24, -44, -14),
  y = c(0, -12, 10, -23, 0)
)

player_zones <- add_zone(player_shots) |>
  group_by(zone) |>
  summarise(attempts = n(), fg_pct = mean(scoring_play), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(zone = as.character(zone)) |>
  left_join(label_spots, by = "zone") |>
  left_join(mutate(select(league_zones, zone, league_fg = fg_pct),
                   zone = as.character(zone)), by = "zone") |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s\n%.0f%% (lg %.0f%%)", zone, 100 * fg_pct, 100 * league_fg))

geom_basketball("wnba", display_range = "defense") +
  geom_point(aes(x, y, color = zone), data = add_zone(player_shots),
             alpha = 0.5, size = 1.4) +
  geom_label(aes(x, y, label = label), data = player_zones, size = 2.6, alpha = 0.9) +
  labs(
    title = paste(top_shooter, "2025: FG% by zone"),
    subtitle = "League FG% in each zone in brackets",
    color = NULL,
    caption = "Data: wehoop::load_wnba_shots()"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The corner-three label covers both corners.

## Women's college basketball

`load_wbb_shots()` returns the same columns for Division I, so every helper
above works unchanged. One difference to watch: the college feed spells shot
types without spaces (`"LayUpShot"`, `"JumpShot"`, `"MadeFreeThrow"`), which is
why the free throw filter is case-insensitive and allows for a missing space.
The 2026 season (2025-26) is large, so subset to one team.

```{r wbb}
wbb_shots <- load_wbb_shots(seasons = 2026)

nrow(wbb_shots)

wbb_team <- wbb_shots |>
  filter(team_name == "South Carolina", !grepl("free ?throw", type_text, ignore.case = TRUE)) |>
  fold_to_left_basket() |>
  add_zone()

nrow(wbb_team)
```

```{r wbb-hex, fig.alt = "Hexbin shot density map of South Carolina's 2025-26 field goal attempts on an NCAA court."}
geom_basketball("ncaa", display_range = "defense") +
  geom_hex(aes(x, y), data = wbb_team, binwidth = c(2, 2), alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#fbe3e8", high = "#73000a", trans = "sqrt") +
  labs(
    title = "South Carolina, 2025-26: shot density",
    fill = "Attempts",
    caption = "Data: wehoop::load_wbb_shots()"
  )
```

```{r wbb-zones}
# The same zone-rule check as for the WNBA
wbb_team |>
  filter(scoring_play) |>
  summarise(agreement = mean(zone_is_three == (score_value == 3)))

wbb_team |>
  group_by(zone) |>
  summarise(attempts = n(), fg_pct = mean(scoring_play), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(share_of_attempts = attempts / sum(attempts))
```

## WNBA Stats API shots and `sdv_court_coords()` {#wnba-stats-api-shots-and-sdv_court_coords}

`load_wnba_stats_shots()` reads the WNBA Stats API's shot chart data from a
GitHub release. It records the exact shot value (`shot_value`), the result
(`shot_result`) and the league's own `shot_distance`, but its locations are in
the legacy stats frame: tenths of a foot, with the origin at the shooter's
basket. [`sdvplotR`](https://sdvplotR.sportsdataverse.org/) converts that frame
into the `sportyR` court frame with `sdv_court_coords()`, which adds `court_x`
and `court_y` in feet with the basket at `x = -41.75`. The `"nba"` provider is
the right one here: stats.wnba.com uses the same frame as stats.nba.com, and the
WNBA court shares the NBA court's 94-foot length and basket position.

```{r stats-shots}
stats_shots <- load_wnba_stats_shots(seasons = 2025) |>
  sdvplotR::sdv_court_coords(x_column = "x_legacy", y_column = "y_legacy")

stats_shots |>
  select(player_name, team_tricode, action_type, shot_value, shot_distance,
         x_legacy, y_legacy, court_x, court_y) |>
  head()
```

```{r stats-chart, fig.alt = "Half-court chart of one team's 2025 WNBA Stats API shots, colored by two-point or three-point attempt."}
stats_team <- stats_shots |> filter(team_tricode == "LVA")

geom_basketball("wnba", display_range = "defense") +
  geom_point(aes(court_x, court_y, color = factor(shot_value)),
             data = stats_team, alpha = 0.35, size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`2` = "#c2bccc", `3` = "#221A4D")) +
  labs(
    title = "Las Vegas Aces, 2025: two- and three-point attempts",
    color = "Shot value",
    caption = "Data: wehoop::load_wnba_stats_shots(), converted with sdvplotR::sdv_court_coords()"
  )
```

Because this table carries the true shot value, you can check zone rules exactly
or use `shot_value` directly. Do not pass ESPN `coordinate_x`/`coordinate_y` to
`sdv_court_coords()`: they are already in feet on the center-court frame.

## Team-colored courts with `sdv_surface()`

`sdvplotR::sdv_surface()` wraps `sportyR::geom_basketball()` and paints the lane
and apron in a team's colors, optionally with its logo at center court
(`center_logo = TRUE`). The `"wnba"` key draws the WNBA court and `"wbb"` the
NCAA court. It needs `sportyR` 2.4.5 or later.

```{r sdv-check, include = FALSE}
sdv_ok <- requireNamespace("sdvplotR", quietly = TRUE) &&
  utils::packageVersion("sportyR") >= "2.4.5"
```

```{r sdv-surface, eval = sdv_ok, fig.alt = "WNBA half court in Las Vegas Aces colors with a hexbin of the team's shots, and a plain NCAA half court with one women's college team's makes and misses."}
library(sdvplotR)

sdv_surface("wnba", team = "LV", display_range = "defense") +
  geom_hex(aes(x, y), data = team_shots, binwidth = c(2, 2), alpha = 0.8)

# Plain NCAA court for women's college basketball
sdv_surface("wbb", display_range = "defense") +
  geom_point(aes(x, y, color = result), data = wbb_team, alpha = 0.4)
```
